standard_prerequisites.name: The flattening setup
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given f,g : B -> A, the coequalizer W generated by c : A -> W and p : prd b:B (c(f b) = c(g b)), a family C : A -> type and a family of equivalences D : prd b:B (C(f b) ~ C(g b)), the family P : W -> type is defined recursively by P(c a) := C a and map P (p b) := ua(D b).
standard_prerequisites.use: The whole lemma is stated over this setup and the retained context is the author's own definition of it.

standard_prerequisites.name: The constructors of W-tilde
standard_prerequisites.statement: W-tilde is generated by c-tilde(a,x) and p-tilde(b,y), and the auxiliary lemma produces c-tilde' into the total space Sigma w:W P(w) together with p-tilde' with its coherence path.
standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma is about a section of a family Q over that total space, so both constructors are inputs to the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dependent paths over the constructors
standard_prerequisites.statement: To define a section of prd x:P(w) Q(w,x) it suffices to give the values and, for each path constructor, a dependent path; the relevant reformulation is thm:dpath-forall.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source line 1885 to turn the goal into a pointwise equation over y : C(f b).

core_obligations: Given Q : (Sigma w:W P(w)) -> type together with c : prd a:A prd x:C a Q(c-tilde'(a,x)) and p : prd b:B prd y:C(f b) (trans (p-tilde'(b,y)) (c(f b,y)) = c(g b, D b y)), produce k : prd z:(Sigma w:W P(w)) Q z with k(c-tilde'(a,x)) := c(a,x) (source lines 1871-1877).
Define k(w,x) by induction on w : W; in the case w := c(a) the input x has type C(a) and the value c(a,x) is available, and this also secures the stated computation rule (source lines 1879-1882).
Check that the definition is preserved by transport along p(b): by thm:dpath-forall it suffices to compare the two sides at any y : C(f b) (source lines 1884-1886).

Rewrite c(g b, trans (p b) y) using the path q : trans (p b) y = D b y supplied by thm:transport-is-given, obtaining a transport along a map of the form x |-> c-tilde'(g b, x) and applying thm:transport-compose (source lines 1887-1895).
Reduce the remaining goal to the composite of the two transports written as p-tilde'(b,y), which is exactly the hypothesis p(b,y) (source lines 1896-1919).

proof_roadmap.step: Define k on the point constructor of W, which also gives the computation rule.
Turn the coherence obligation into a pointwise equation by thm:dpath-forall and introduce the path q from thm:transport-is-given.
Compute the transported value along c-tilde'(g b, -) using thm:transport-compose.
Transport the right-hand side across and identify the composite of the two transports with p-tilde'(b,y), closing by the hypothesis p(b,y).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.12.4 at source lines 1870-1877: a dependent recursion principle for the total space Sigma w:W P(w), where P is defined recursively along the path constructor of W. The proof (source lines 1878-1920) is one of the technical core steps of the flattening lemma and is not a citation: the definition is produced by induction on W at lines 1879-1882, and the coherence obligation is then reworked through three separate manoeuvres, thm:dpath-forall at line 1885, the transport computation with the path q from thm:transport-is-given at line 1887, and thm:transport-compose at line 1894, before the two transports can be combined into p-tilde'(b,y) at lines 1901-1919 and the hypothesis p(b,y) can be applied. The statement records none of these steps and the lemma is stated for an arbitrary family Q over the total space.
